# the contributor audit: coefficient obstruction and actual full-star rigidity

Sources:
`candidate 4c13e7d95b295d25` and
`candidate 9384183373b50261`.


actual convex families. The general zero-slack case remains unresolved.

## Binary coefficients and the exact 43-node obstruction

The terminating recursion defines an integral affine coefficient vector
even if roots are affinely dependent. Its parity is the unit vector of
the designated root color. Iteration of the prescribed midpoint parent
preserves the set of positive coordinates. Termination at one unit vector
therefore forces exactly one positive coordinate. Writing the others as
negative integers, the unique-odd-coordinate rule is exactly the condition
that their binary supports are pairwise disjoint; the parent discards the
least significant digit. Both directions of this equivalence are proved.

The ternary tree has exactly the asserted 43 distinct nodes. Its unit
linear radii satisfy the root-maximality and coefficient-space norm tie
rules. Each table cap has its displayed exact integer trace count; the
ten permutation orbits cover the whole source. The root reran the plain
Python verifier, which prints the five separate contributions to each
trace: PASS. Thus every node has a closed containing cap of mass at most
seven, strictly below 43/4. No exact maximum of seven is inferred.

The missing point in the square projection is inside the projected hull
and is not in the projected source. Thus that projection is not an actual
complete positive-fiber support. Uniform radii also do not preserve the
nonaffine coefficient graph in a common-origin homothetic model. These
are material obstructions, not discarded technicalities.

## Full-star rigidity for actual fibers

Replacing the body by the hull of its positive fibers preserves every
positive fiber. Every real fiber over their base hull contains a positive
Minkowski combination and is full-dimensional. Forest recursion puts the
base affine hull equal to that of the roots. The full symmetric midpoint
star spans this affine hull and places its root in the relative interior.

The ordinary volume-root and, independently, each actual support-function
profile are finite concave functions there. They therefore have global
affine supporting majorants at the common root. In each exact midpoint
pair the two nonnegative majorant gaps sum to zero. Both gaps vanish, so
one common majorant saturates every root. This proves affine radii and,
using the homothetic support formula in coordinate directions, affine
centroids. Radius affinity alone would not justify the latter step.

Backward recursion propagates both affine identities through the entire
finite forest. The centroid graph is consequently an affine copy of its
lattice-convex base support. Weighted relative Doignon applies in the
saturated base lattice of rank m, giving one actual graph point of weighted
depth at least T/2^m. The proof using convex hulls of heavy finite subsets
correctly handles strict complements and all closed containing caps.
Counting only fibers whose actual centroid lies in the cap and applying
ordinary Grunbaum yields Gamma_d T/2^m, with m<=n.

The dimension-zero base is handled separately. Continuous fibers remain
positive full-dimensional throughout this theorem. Arbitrary positive
graph weights are permitted, and the final OC specialization uses the
original fiber-volume weights.

The rank obstruction in the final section correctly concerns an affine
embedding of the full coefficient affine span. Finite-set injectivity
alone does not preserve affine dimension. Separately, a cap-preserving
realization on the same 43 unit-weight nodes is excluded by the weighted
bound. If completion adds nodes, their actual masses enter all budgets.
The theorem does not remove the full-star hypothesis or classify general
forests.
